title: Stage 2 ION business case direction for Cambridge
subtitle: Committee also heard MobilityPLUS accessible transit overview, emergency ramps, bus rapid transit costing and a Dundas route feasibility review.
overview: The Planning and Works Committee held a special meeting on Stage 2 ION, the proposed light rail extension to Cambridge. After education sessions and debate, it recommended that staff include three project alternatives from report TSD-RTS-23-001 in the Stage 2 business case {{vote:m4}}. Staff were also asked to add emergency ramps, a fourth option starting construction in south Cambridge, and a version with the terminus in east Cambridge. They will report on the feasibility of a route down Dundas.

In a separate motion, the committee recommended that bus rapid transit (BRT) also be considered and costed {{vote:m5}}. The business case will inform a future funding request to senior governments, so the options set now shape what Council can later choose from.

Earlier, staff gave an education session on MobilityPLUS, the specialized transit service. Staff plan to add drivers, revise seating on new buses and renew the service's business plan this year. The committee also went into closed session on legal advice about land disposition and litigation. The minutes report no public outcome from it. These are recommendations to Council.

decisions.detail: The committee agreed to take up the Stage 2 ION status report at this special meeting rather than waiting for the June 6 meeting.

decisions.item: Three project alternatives in business case
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff include the three alternatives described in report TSD-RTS-23-001 in the Stage 2 ION business case.
The committee recommended that staff add emergency ramps to the business case, so riders with disabilities can leave a stopped train without a platform.
The committee recommended a fourth alternative running from the south terminus in Cambridge to Preston, with construction starting in south Cambridge.
The committee recommended adding a T4 option with the terminus in east Cambridge rather than downtown, and asked staff for information on the feasibility of a Dundas route.
The committee recommended that BRT be considered and costed in the Stage 2 ION business case.

debate: Supporters said Cambridge should get its fair share of rapid transit and that delay raises costs. They also cited economic development, environmental benefits and a letter from business groups urging action.

Some councillors worried about the escalated cost estimate of about $4.46 billion and whether senior governments would fund it. Others said funding could be reassessed later and that building the business case should not wait.
Staff defended the 20% contingency as standard at this early stage, since there are no boreholes, utility investigations or bridge designs yet. Staff said it would fall as design advances.

One Cambridge councillor questioned the downtown route. The concern was that dedicating a lane to LRT on Hespeler Road and downtown streets would take away road space, and that growth is heading south and east. Staff said the corridor is meant to become pedestrian-friendly and dense, and that a Dundas route would likely score poorly. They also said a new rail alignment could take one to two years of added work.

Councillors asked about starting with BRT or building Cambridge first. Staff said a disconnected system would hurt ridership through transfers, and that converting BRT to LRT is hard if structures are involved. Another councillor raised accessibility, asking for emergency ramps so riders with disabilities are not stranded.
